design.quote: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SCORED Randomized Controlled Trial.

population.value: Patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate renal impairment who are at cardiovascular risk
population.quote: SCORED (Effect of Sotagliflozin on Cardiovascular and Renal Events in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Moderate Renal Impairment Who Are at Cardiovascular Risk) was a randomized trial in diabetes with kidney disease

sample_size.quote: There were 741 patients (7%) in stage A, 6560 (62%) in stage B (pre-HF), and 3283 (31%) in stage C/D (established HF).

intervention.quote: comparing sotagliflozin versus placebo on cardiovascular death, HF hospitalizations, and urgent HF visits

comparator.quote: comparing sotagliflozin versus placebo on cardiovascular death, HF hospitalizations, and urgent HF visits

primary_findings.quote: Increasing HF stage was associated with a 2- to 4-fold increase in the primary outcome/major adverse cardiovascular events in the placebo group.
primary_findings.outcome: Primary composite (cardiovascular death and HF-related events) / major adverse cardiovascular events

primary_findings.quote: The kidney-specific composite was 5-fold higher in stage B (pre-HF) versus stage A but similar in stages B and C/D.
primary_findings.outcome: Kidney-specific composite (≥50% decline in eGFR, kidney failure, or kidney death)

primary_findings.quote: The effect of sotagliflozin versus placebo was similar, irrespective of HF stage (primary outcome: hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.88]; Pinteraction=1.00)
primary_findings.outcome: Primary composite (cardiovascular death and HF-related events)

primary_findings.quote: with higher absolute benefit in each HF stage (P-trendIRR=0.002)
primary_findings.outcome: Primary composite (cardiovascular death and HF-related events) - absolute benefit

primary_findings.quote: The absolute benefit for the kidney-specific end point was comparable for stages B and C/D.
